change.author: Joe Au-Yeung

findings.title: Google credential is saved as the safeParse result object, not the token
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`, see parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29). Line 97 assigns that to `key`, and line 100 writes it to `credential.key`. After the first token refresh the stored key is `{ success: true, data: {...} }`. The old code stored the parsed data. The next `GoogleCalendarService` constructor then calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) and throws, so every Google Calendar credential breaks after its first refresh. Use `parsed.data` and check `parsed.success`, as the Zoom and Salesforce call sites do.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: Line 96 calls `prisma.credential.update`. The file has no `prisma` import (the only match for `prisma` in the file is this line). It fails type-check, and at runtime it throws a ReferenceError inside `getClient`. That rejects `this.conn`, so every Salesforce calendar operation fails. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

findings.title: Salesforce now refreshes on every instantiation, then builds the connection with the old access token
findings.body: `getClient` runs in the constructor (line 57). The new code POSTs to Salesforce's token endpoint on every instantiation, whether or not the token is expired. It stores the new token (line 96), but the `jsforce.Connection` at lines 101-108 still uses `credentialKey.access_token` from before the refresh. So the refresh buys nothing for the current request, and it adds a network call and a possible rate-limit hit per instantiation. `response.statusText !== "OK"` (line 86) also throws for any response with an empty status text (e.g. HTTP/2). Salesforce is also the only provider that bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync does not apply to it, yet it still calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Refresh only when expired, use the new `access_token` for the connection, and route the call through `refreshOAuthTokens`. Also confirm that adding a refresh to Salesforce is intended in this PR.

findings.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys that evaluate to "[object Object]"
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are both the string `"[object Object]"`, because zod types do not override `toString`. The schema is therefore `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown | optional }`. The second key overwrites the first, so there is no number requirement and no expiry check. `z.object` also strips unknown keys by default, so `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `scope` and the like never reach `data`. In credential-sync mode the consumers read fields that are gone: Zoom computes `Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000`, which is NaN (zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts:122), and Office365 loses `expires_in`. The result is an unusable stored key or a refresh on every call. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` plus an explicit expiry check, for example `.refine` over any numeric field, or require a named field.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token overwrites the real one, in non-sync mode too
findings.body: When the response has no `refresh_token`, the helper sets the literal string `"refresh_token"`. This runs outside credential-sync mode as well. Office365 calendar's schema has `refresh_token` optional (office365calendar CalendarService.ts:56), and its caller spreads the parsed data over the stored credentials (line 264). A refresh response without a new refresh token therefore replaces the stored valid refresh token with the literal `"refresh_token"`, and the credential cannot refresh again. Previously the old value survived the spread. Apply the placeholder only in sync mode, or have callers keep the existing refresh token.

findings.title: In sync mode a raw fetch Response is returned to callers that expect an axios/SDK/googleapis shape
findings.body:
The sync branch returns the `fetch` `Response`, but several callers read a different shape from it:
- Google reads `res?.data` (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:94). `Response` has no `data`, so it throws a TypeError, which is swallowed (the catch returns the old auth, line 108).
- Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `.data.error` and `.data.access_token` (zohocrm CalendarService.ts:217; zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:96).
- HubSpot reads `.expiresIn` and `.accessToken` directly on the result (hubspot CalendarService.ts:192).

None of them calls `.json()`. Only callers that run `handle*Response` or `handleErrorsJson` on the response work in sync mode. Normalise the sync response inside the helper, or have each caller adapt it.

findings.title: Sync endpoint request is unauthenticated, has no timeout, and the status is unchecked
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared secret or header. It has no timeout, and a non-2xx response is not checked here. Any party that can reach the endpoint can request tokens for an arbitrary userId. An error body is also passed on as if it were a token response. Consider sending the webhook secret (or a signed header), setting a timeout, and failing on `!response.ok`.

findings.title: Credential id is passed where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects the user id
findings.body: The third argument of `refreshOAuthTokens` is `userId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3). Here `credentialId` (`credential.id`, line 53) is passed. In sync mode this asks the sync endpoint for the wrong user's tokens, because a credential id is not a user id. It also skips the intended `userId` null check. Pass `credential.userId`; `biginAuth` has the credential in scope and must pass it down to `refreshAccessToken`.

findings.title: Dead `success` check and removed error logging change behaviour on invalid MS responses
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws when parsing fails and otherwise always returns `success: true`. So `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` is always `data`. The removed `console.error` branch (which logged the zod error and the MS response) is gone, so a malformed MS response now throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" error without the response body. Previously it was logged and the old credentials were kept. Simplify the spread and keep the diagnostic log.

findings.title: Body validation and decryption errors become unhandled 500s; secret compared non-constant-time; no method check
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` (line 31), `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` (lines 57-59) all throw on bad input. Nothing catches them, so a malformed request, wrong key or bad ciphertext gives a 500 instead of a 400. Use `safeParse` and a try/catch that returns 400. The secret check (lines 24-27) uses `!==` on a string, which is not timing-safe, so use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. The handler also accepts any HTTP method, so restrict it to POST. The decrypted `keys` are written to `credential.key` (lines 78, 85) without any per-app shape validation. A bad payload would silently corrupt a user's credential.

findings.title: Unrelated hard-coded slug in redirectUri
findings.body: `appConfig.slug` was replaced by the literal `zoho-bigin` in `redirectUri`, while `appConfig` is still imported and used for `getAppKeysFromSlug(appConfig.slug)` (line 12) and the scope (line 22). The change has nothing to do with credential sync and adds a second source of truth for the slug. Revert it.

findings.title: No tests for the new webhook or the refresh helpers
findings.body: The PR adds a credential-write webhook, a token-response parser and a refresh wrapper used by about ten integrations. It adds no tests. A unit test of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` would have caught the bugs in this file and the Google misuse (Google CalendarService.ts:97).

contracts.action: New webhook that creates or overwrites a user's app credential
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing OAuth callbacks create credentials via createOAuthAppCredential (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts), which checks the session user and team admin access.
contracts.before_after: The callbacks validate the authenticated user. The webhook trusts a shared secret header and a body userId, with no session. It then does findFirst and update/create on prisma.credential.
contracts.visible_effect: The user's connected app uses the externally supplied keys on the next use. There is no UI feedback.
contracts.failure_mode: Invalid body, bad ciphertext or bad JSON throws and returns a 500 (lines 31, 57-59). The caller sees an error; nothing is stored. Anyone holding the secret can overwrite any user's credentials for any app.

contracts.action: refreshOAuthTokens replaces direct provider refresh calls in ~10 integrations
contracts.equivalent_path: Each integration's previous inline fetch/axios/SDK refresh call.
contracts.before_after: Before, the refresh response was passed straight to the provider-specific handler. Now, in sync mode, a raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint is returned to handlers expecting axios, SDK or googleapis shapes. In non-sync mode behaviour is unchanged, except that parseRefreshTokenResponse now wraps Google, Office365 and Zoom parsing.
contracts.visible_effect: In sync mode Google, HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin refreshes fail. Google and Zoho CRM errors are logged or swallowed. In non-sync mode the Google credential is corrupted by the safeParse-object write.
contracts.failure_mode: Google swallows the error and keeps the expired token; Zoho Bigin throws from `.data.error` on a Response, uncaught.

contracts.action: Salesforce getClient now refreshes the token via fetch and updates the credential on every service construction
contracts.equivalent_path: Other services refresh only when the token is expired (e.g. zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts:137-139) and build their client from the refreshed token.
contracts.before_after: Before, getClient built a jsforce Connection directly from the stored key. Now it always refreshes and writes to the DB, then builds the connection from the stale stored access token. prisma is not imported.
contracts.visible_effect: Salesforce bookings fail with a ReferenceError before the connection is built.
contracts.failure_mode: The rejected promise in the constructor (`this.conn = this.getClient(...)`) is unhandled until awaited. Any later `await this.conn` throws.

summary: The change adds credential syncing, but it has two merge-blocking bugs, both found by reading the code (nothing was run). The Google refresh stores the zod `safeParse` result object as the credential key, which corrupts every Google Calendar credential after its first refresh. The Salesforce `getClient` uses `prisma` without importing it, so every Salesforce calendar operation fails. Beyond those, in sync mode `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built from keys that all evaluate to \"[object Object]\", and it strips fields such as `expires_in`. In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch Response to callers that expect axios, SDK or googleapis shapes. Zoho Bigin passes the credential id where the user id is expected. The parser writes a placeholder `refresh_token` even outside sync mode, and in Office365 calendar that overwrites a stored valid refresh token. The new webhook returns a 500 on bad input and compares the secret without a timing-safe check. The PR adds no tests. The import moves into `_utils/oauth/` look consistent, and no stale import paths remain.
